summary.intent: Resolve automated PR review comments from Copilot and CodeRabbit on PR #392, then fix the release gate so it blocks merging until E2E tests pass on main (not just for release-please PRs).
summary.outcome: All 3 review comments on PR #392 were fixed, committed, and resolved. PR #394 was created to fix the release gate by adding a ci-e2e.yml orchestrator with unified change detection and a retrigger job that re-runs the release gate on open release-please PRs after every main merge.

repo: The release gate only enforced E2E checks for release-please branches; non-release PRs auto-passed with 'Not a release PR — E2E gate not applicable', making the required check meaningless for feature branches.
E2E workflow (e2e.yml) previously triggered on every push to main regardless of what changed, unlike desktop-e2e.yml which already used dorny/paths-filter for conditional execution.
Committed fixture files live in tests/web-e2e/fixtures/files/ and test helper functions could overwrite/delete them if the requested filename matched a fixture name — no guard existed.
The project uses a .planning/ directory with per-phase PLAN.md, SUMMARY.md, RESEARCH.md, and VERIFICATION.md files, plus a .learnings/ directory for dated markdown files.
desktop-e2e.yml already had the dorny/paths-filter + conditional job pattern that e2e.yml lacked.
The project is FSM1/cipher-box, a monorepo with apps/web, apps/api, packages/crypto, packages/core, packages/api-client, packages/sdk, packages/sdk-core.

code.finding: createTestMediaFile, createTestImageFile, createTestTextFile, and createTestBinaryFile all lacked a COMMITTED_FIXTURES guard — cleanup would delete committed fixture files if a test used the same filename.
Missing faro_enabled: true metadata field that was required by the schema/plan.
page.evaluate() called in teardown without page.isClosed() guard, causing errors when the page was already closed.
jq // empty pattern returns empty string which causes gh CLI to error; also log message said 'Web E2E' while polling ci-e2e.yml. Fixed to use // "" and updated log message.
Desktop paths-filter was missing Cargo.lock, which would cause desktop E2E to not trigger on Rust dependency updates.
gh run rerun on a stale release-please SHA means detect-changes diff against HEAD would use stale checkout; fixed to diff against origin/main instead.

workflow: When gh run rerun is used to retrigger a workflow, the checkout SHA is the original trigger SHA — path filters using HEAD..PREV_TAG produce stale diffs; always diff against origin/main when re-run semantics matter.
dorny/paths-filter is the established pattern in this repo for conditional job execution based on changed paths.

The resolve-pr-reviews skill follows a strict workflow: fetch unresolved GraphQL threads → read code → triage → fix → typecheck → commit → reply via REST (--field for integer in_reply_to) → resolve via GraphQL mutation.
Multiple parallel background polling tasks with sleep loops is noisy and hard to track; the approach worked but generated many orphaned task notifications.
CodeRabbit has per-PR quota limits that can impose ~23 minute cooldowns between review runs.
workflow_call reusable workflows inherit vars context from the calling repository automatically — no special handling needed.

friction: CodeRabbit was rate-limited for ~23 minutes, requiring ~40 minutes of polling before its review arrived.

Initial diagnosis of the release gate problem was wrong twice — first proposed adding E2E to feature PRs, then proposed retriggering after merge, before understanding the actual issue was stale green checks on release-please PRs.
Background polling with many parallel sleep tasks created a flood of task completion notifications that cluttered the session.
Finding the correct REST comment IDs for replying to review threads required multiple gh API calls and trial/error.
gh run rerun with the stale SHA issue was subtle — only caught by CodeRabbit, not during implementation.
open_items: PR #394 (ci-e2e.yml orchestrator + retrigger-release-gate) needs to be reviewed and merged.

The retrigger logic uses gh run rerun which re-runs the entire previous workflow run — if the release gate run was triggered by a different event context, this may have unexpected side effects worth monitoring.
